text: Gov't rolls out action plan to attract and develop talent in key sectors

Under its Resolution 336/NQ-CP, dated October 23, 2026, the Vietnamese Government has adopted an action plan to implement Conclusion No. 105-KL/TW, dated October 15, 2026, of the 14th Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam on attracting and effectively utilizing talent in key sectors and fields.

According to the Government News, the Government will develop a national framework for identifying talent, introduce special policies to attract and retain outstanding individuals, and strengthen training and research capacity in strategic sectors in favor of Vietnam's rapid and sustainable development.

Under the action plan, the Ministry of Home Affairs will be responsible for coordinating with relevant ministries and agencies to draft a resolution on special mechanisms and policies for talent development and utilization and submit it to the National Assembly for consideration and approval.

The Government will develop an open and flexible national framework for identifying talent, combining general standards with specific criteria tailored to different groups, sectors, fields and assignments.
Existing regulations on attracting, recruiting, employing and rewarding talented individuals across the political system will also be reviewed and revised to ensure consistency with the new policies.

The plan calls for further improvements to policies on salaries, housing, land and decentralization of authority in talent-related matters, with priority given to mountainous, border, maritime and island areas.

A national talent database, an indicator system and an information portal will be established to facilitate the assessment, verification, updating, connection, sharing and use of talent-related data, while ensuring consistency, information security and personal data protection.
Mechanisms will also be strengthened to manage risks and assess and protect individuals undertaking innovation activities for the common good.
Transparent arrangements will be introduced to recognize and honor national talent based on tangible contributions.

In addition, administrative procedures for international talent and their family members will be streamlined through coordinated processes with clearly defined responsibilities and processing deadlines.

The Ministry of Science and Technology will coordinate with the Ministry of Home Affairs and relevant agencies to identify and regularly update priority sectors, strategic tasks, programs, projects, key works, major national challenges and breakthrough initiatives requiring talented personnel.

Digital platforms and technological tools will be developed to identify talent, connect candidates with suitable opportunities, forecast demand and coordinate talent deployment, while avoiding overlapping investments and safeguarding data security.
Investment will focus on leading research teams, national key laboratories, strategic technology centers, specialized innovation hubs and high-performance computing centers.

Sandbox mechanisms will be applied to selected arrangements for assigning tasks, recruiting and rewarding talent, providing financing, managing intellectual property and granting access to research infrastructure.
The Ministry of Education and Training will lead the development of a program under which leading experts mentor and guide younger generations of talent.
Early identification, selection, training and development schemes will be introduced for different groups and priority fields, with particular attention to talented school and university students.
The program will support scientists, engineers, managers, young entrepreneurs and highly skilled workers in meeting international standards.
Training will be closely linked to research, innovation and practical needs, with long-term support for career development.
Outstanding scientists and young talent will be selected for training and research at leading foreign universities, research institutes and technology corporations.
The outcomes of overseas training will be aligned with domestic development priorities, research results and the practical application of knowledge and technology.
Selected universities, research institutes, key laboratories and innovation centers will be upgraded to regional and international standards.
Centers of excellence and hubs for talent development and networking will also be established.
The Ministry of Finance will lead efforts to formulate special financial policies to attract and effectively utilize talent.
Annual state budget for talent development is expected to reach around 0.1 percent of GDP within the overall funding framework for science, technology, innovation and digital transformation.
Localities with financial autonomy may decide to allocate higher amounts.

Financial policies will encourage businesses across all economic sectors to identify, nominate, recruit, employ and develop talent, while co-financing training, research and innovation in strategic sectors and emerging and high technologies.
Ministries, agencies and localities will integrate talent development into their strategies and socio-economic development plans.
Their performance in attracting, nurturing and effectively deploying talent will serve as a basis for assessing the accountability of organizations and their leaders.

The action plan also emphasizes the need to expand international cooperation networks and initiatives to engage overseas Vietnamese and international experts in training, consultancy, research, technology transfer and the implementation of strategic tasks and projects in Vietnam.
